candidates.summary: Young adult care-leavers have a death rate about four times higher than the general population

candidates.lead: Young adult care-leavers have a death rate about four times higher than the general population
candidates.evidence_text: Teen who went into care at 10 calls system 'fundamentally flawed' - BBC News Image caption, Hayden said he would like to see significant changes in the care system By Lauren Hirst North West Published 25 minutes ago A teenager who went into care when he was 10 has described how he struggled to navigate the system and seek help. Hayden, now aged 17, lived in a children's home until he was 16 before moving into a semi-independent home. After feeling unsafe there he ended up sofa-surfing. "There is an incredible amount of individuals working so hard to improve the lives of young people but the system is fundamentally flawed," said Hayden, who got in touch with the BBC via Your Voice to share his experience. A new government-commissioned report found that young adult care-leavers have a death rate about four times higher than the general population . The report noted the potentially catastrophic consequences for those who are often left alone "with no safety net". People leaving care in England at 18 often lose "significant levers of support", the report concluded, as it warned the so-called "care cliff" must be addressed. "You kind of are navigating it by yourself and just hoping you've said the right things and put the right things forward to make things happen," said Hayden, who grew up in Middleton, Greater Manchester, before being placed in care in a different local authority area. "We are not the undeserving poor of the Victorian era. "People deserve compassion because they have been through so much." 'It wasn't easy' Hayden, who turns 18 next month, is currently living in a semi-independent placement in Oldham while studying at a sixth-form college. He said he hoped to remain there while focusing on his A-levels in government and politics, economics and biology. "There's quite a bit of legislation that says if moving will cause a detriment to your education that you should be able to remain in the placement. "So that's what I've fought for, but it wasn't easy - it took a while." Hayden said he would like to see changes to way the care system operates. "I think the biggest thing for me is removing the profit motive from children's homes because there is no place for profit in improving the lives of children that have nowhere else to go," he said. "It's just something that you simply can't do. "So I would like to see homes brought back under local authority control, so that there is a closer eye on the most vulnerable members of society and so that schools and homes can work together effectively to improve the lives of young children." The government previously said it was driving forward a national rollout of connected housing options for those leaving care, starting with £25m this year. It said this would "significantly increase" young people's chances of being offered a "home that provides them with community and connection rather than leaving them isolated in inappropriate accommodation". If you've been affected by the issues in this story, you can find information, advice and support from the BBC's Action Line . Anyone feeling emotionally distressed or suicidal can call Samaritans for free on 116 123 or visit samaritans.org in the UK. candidates.evidence_text: When World War One broke out in 1914, Wilfred Wood was working on the railways as a shed cleaner But by the end of 1916, he had enlisted in the Cheshire Regiment of the British Army where he trained as a stretcher bearer to collect the wounded from the battlefields He was then transferred to the 10th Battalion Northumberland Fusiliers where he would later take part in one of the last battles of the World War One involving British soldiers fighting in Italy The Battle of Vittorio Veneto was fought from 24 October to 3 November 1918 and was seen as a decisive victory that contributed to the end of the war Mark Smith, who is a medals specialist at Stanley Gibbons Baldwins, said Wood went above and beyond what was expected of him and used his own initiative when his unit was held up by hostile machine guns and snipers The Stockport shed cleaner given the Victoria Cross

candidates.evidence_text: The street outside legendary indie club 42s, a front garden on Burnage Lane and a pub's function room with a tiny stage - all locations in Manchester where you could have found Courteeners in their early days The four school friends from Middleton, near Rochdale, have certainly come a long way since they hit the Manchester indie scene in 2006 While they have travelled around the world ever since, there is no place like home and they will take to the stage later for a huge homecoming gig at Wythenshawe Park From humble beginnings performing for friends in the garden of their shared house in Burnage, the Courteeners are now celebrating 20 years together Fresh from releasing a new best-of compilation album called God Bless The Band, lead singer and songwriter Liam Fray spoke to BBC North West Tonight at The Briton's Protection pub on Deansgate, where he first performed as a solo artist back in 2005 Sitting upstairs in the pub, Fray smiled at the 3ft (0.9m) stage and single spotlight on the ceiling while recalling the night he spent there more than two decades ago

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Combined Authority The top boss running Greater Manchester - for now - in £245k role An interim chief has been appointed. News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 07:30, 30 Aug 2026 View 2 Images The Tootal buildings in Manchester An interim top boss has been chosen to run Greater Manchester alongside mayor Bev Craig after the previous chief executive was poached to work in Number 10 North Andrew Lightfoot’s name was put forward on Friday (August 30) to step up from his job as deputy to formally become interim group chief executive at the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA), which also includes Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service The post comes with a wage of £245,000 and serves as the GMCA’s head of paid service - its most senior officer - as well as returning officer and director general of Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) The recommendation needs to be approved on September 25 while the search for a permanent chief begins Former GMCA boss Caroline Simpson stepped down in July to join Andy Burnham's team at Heron House in the Prime Minister’s Manchester office, which opened an ‘immediate gap’ to be plugged at the Combined Authority

candidates.evidence_text: Wigan 'They wouldn't let an animal suffer like this. It's my life, I should be able to choose what happens to it' Brian Griffin has incurable blood cancer. With the assisted dying bill - the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill - set to be debated News Iram Ramzan 07:00, 30 Aug 2026 Updated 07:19, 30 Aug 2026 Standing proud at almost 6ft at his home on a quiet cul-de-sac where he lives with wife Denise, it's hard to believe Brian Griffin is terminally ill. There's little to immediately suggest he is living on borrowed time For decades, Brian was a familiar figure at the front of the classroom, teaching biology and advanced skills to thousands of children across Wigan Among them were his own son and daughter, before he went on to lecture at the University of Manchester . Now the 74-year-old from Bryn is preparing to die, spending much of his remaining days considering how that will happen Brian invited the Manchester Evening News to his home to discuss the assisted dying bill - the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill - which will be debated in the Commons once again next month "If this Bill is passed, then in 30 years' time people will look back thinking 'they just used to let these people suffer - why?'," Brian says. "And I think people will just look back at it as absolutely barbaric."

About ten minutes later, the crew member who was guarding the door was pushed by one of them, then around 20 to 25 youths ran in, some with knives."

British Transport Police (BTP) said they were called at 3.18pm on Saturday, August 29, to reports a train had struck a van at a level crossing in Burscough One person was in the van and a man was pronounced dead at the scene, the force said . Two passengers who were on the train received treatment for minor injuries Enquiries remain ongoing as BTP has urged anyone with further information to contact police Images shared online show a Northern train that has stopped next to green fields. candidates.evidence_text: Wigan 'Growing up with Wigan bogeyman inspired my own love of horror' Author David Barnett's childhood growing up in Ince, Wigan, inspired his own horror stories Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 16:32, 29 Aug 2026 Updated 16:41, 29 Aug 202 As horror aficionados know, classic folk horror is often set in the isolated countryside - where the natural landscape, archaic traditions and rituals and the dark power of nature lend themselves to the genre But for writer David Barnett, his folk horror is born from the red-brick terraces and slagheaps of Wigan. Growing up in Ince-in-Makerfield , one of his earliest recollections of folk-horror-type lore is the childhood memory of Red Clogs – the Wigan bogeyman who haunts the local c The story goes that Red Clogs is the ghost of a tragic miner who was killed in an accident. The legend says the sound of his distinctive clogs could be heard after dark while walking near the old industrial and pit sites “It's interesting because I did a little bit of research when I was writing, and people in different parts of Wigan had a slightly different version of Red Clogs,” David said. “But it was always a spirit or a ghost or a presence that haunted mining communities “And it varied between being a ghost of a miner who was killed or a malevolent spirit who killed people or kidnapped kids. But the unifying feature was where the name came from. Its clogs were red because they were dripping with blood, usually from kicking someone to death

News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 07:30, 30 Aug 2026 View 2 Images The Tootal buildings in Manchester An interim top boss has been chosen to run Greater Manchester alongside mayor Bev Craig after the previous chief executive was poached to work in Number 10 North Andrew Lightfoot’s name was put forward on Friday (August 30) to step up from his job as deputy to formally become interim group chief executive at the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA), which also includes Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service The post comes with a wage of £245,000 and serves as the GMCA’s head of paid service - its most senior officer - as well as returning officer and director general of Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) The recommendation needs to be approved on September 25 while the search for a permanent chief begins Former GMCA boss Caroline Simpson stepped down in July to join Andy Burnham's team at Heron House in the Prime Minister’s Manchester office, which opened an ‘immediate gap’ to be plugged at the Combined Authority

candidates.evidence_text: Wigan 'They wouldn't let an animal suffer like this. It's my life, I should be able to choose what happens to it' Brian Griffin has incurable blood cancer. With the assisted dying bill - the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill - set to be debated News Iram Ramzan 07:00, 30 Aug 2026 Updated 07:19, 30 Aug 2026 Standing proud at almost 6ft at his home on a quiet cul-de-sac where he lives with wife Denise, it's hard to believe Brian Griffin is terminally ill. There's little to immediately suggest he is living on borrowed time For decades, Brian was a familiar figure at the front of the classroom, teaching biology and advanced skills to thousands of children across Wigan Among them were his own son and daughter, before he went on to lecture at the University of Manchester . Now the 74-year-old from Bryn is preparing to die, spending much of his remaining days considering how that will happen Brian invited the Manchester Evening News to his home to discuss the assisted dying bill - the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill - which will be debated in the Commons once again next month "If this Bill is passed, then in 30 years' time people will look back thinking 'they just used to let these people suffer - why?'," Brian says. "And I think people will just look back at it as absolutely barbaric."

candidates.evidence_text: Rochdale Taco Bell horror as boy stabbed in toilets after '25 youths ran in with knives' before diners desperately saved victim's life Police cordoned off Taco Bell in Rochdale after the attack with a major investigation underway News Amy Walker Court A 13-year-old boy has been left with serious injuries after being stabbed in Taco Bell in Rochdale . Officers from Greater Manchester Police were called to reports of the serious incident at around 6pm on Saturday, August 19, at the restaurant on Riverside Walk A boy, aged 13, was taken to hospital with serious injuries. Two teenage boys have since been arrested on suspicion of assault and possession of a bladed article. Enquiries are ongoing, GMP say A man and his family, who were dining at the restaurant, witnessed the incident. Speaking to the Manchester Evening News , David Lane told of the 'horrific moment' and how his actions helped save the boy "We sat down and ordered our food at around 5.50pm, then a load of kids came in and started fighting," he said. "I got up and went to one of the crew members at Taco Bell and asked them to kick them out because my family were there "I told them to lock the door, and they never did. About ten minutes later, the crew member who was guarding the door was pushed by one of them, then around 20 to 25 youths ran in, some with knives."

candidates.evidence_text: Wigan 'Growing up with Wigan bogeyman inspired my own love of horror' Author David Barnett's childhood growing up in Ince, Wigan, inspired his own horror stories Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 16:32, 29 Aug 2026 Updated 16:41, 29 Aug 202 As horror aficionados know, classic folk horror is often set in the isolated countryside - where the natural landscape, archaic traditions and rituals and the dark power of nature lend themselves to the genre But for writer David Barnett, his folk horror is born from the red-brick terraces and slagheaps of Wigan. Growing up in Ince-in-Makerfield , one of his earliest recollections of folk-horror-type lore is the childhood memory of Red Clogs – the Wigan bogeyman who haunts the local c The story goes that Red Clogs is the ghost of a tragic miner who was killed in an accident. The legend says the sound of his distinctive clogs could be heard after dark while walking near the old industrial and pit sites “It's interesting because I did a little bit of research when I was writing, and people in different parts of Wigan had a slightly different version of Red Clogs,” David said. “But it was always a spirit or a ghost or a presence that haunted mining communities “And it varied between being a ghost of a miner who was killed or a malevolent spirit who killed people or kidnapped kids. But the unifying feature was where the name came from. Its clogs were red because they were dripping with blood, usually from kicking someone to death

candidates.evidence_text: Fires Two months of raging wildfires near Greater Manchester, finally over but not forgotten The M.E.N takes a look back at the devastating fires at Dovestone and Swineshaw, Tintwistle and Saddleworth this summer View 11 Images A hazy view of Manchest News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 15:50, 29 Aug 2026 The huge raging wildfires that broke out near Greater Manchester this summer are finally extinguished Hundreds of firefighters battled blazes at Dovestone and Swineshaw, Tintwistle and Saddleworth with two major incidents declared in July. As the blazes took hold of the vast moorland areas, parts of Greater Manchester, including in some areas miles away, were left covered in smok The wildfires smouldered amid several heatwaves, with very little respite from hot and dry weather. Miles of scorched moorland and devastated wildlife has been left behind In the wake of the wildfires, and the hundreds that have broken out across the country this summer, concerns have been raised over tougher consequences for those who start them with most beginning 'due to human activities'. candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Pride When the rain will stop today in Manchester as 2026 Pride takes place in city centre Met Office forecasts show that the rain is set to persist throughout Saturday afternoon Comments News Miranda Pell Search and Discover Writer 13:08, August Bank Holiday weekend has gotten off to a very wet start, with festivals and other major events taking place all over the UK It comes after the UK has seen an uncharacteristically dry and hot summer, with record-breaking heatwaves and droughts. So for some, this rain is welcome. But for others, it could do with stopping until the end of the long bank holiday weekend Manchester Village Pride 2026 is taking place in the city centre today, after celebrations got underway on Friday, August 28. The parade is taking place from 12pm and then the party will continue in the village until the late hours This year's LGBTQ+ event was created following the voluntary liqudation of the company behind Manchester Pride last year. As a result, a new Community Interest Company (CIC) was founded, with a new focus on the community and with the support of the many venues and bars that make Reiterating the core message behind the new-look event, this year's Parade will take on the theme of 'No Place Like Home'. Not only serving as a nod to queer classic The Wizard of Oz, it will also hone in on the special meaning of home and belonging within a chosen family

candidates.evidence_text: Salford Man fights for life following Salford flats balcony plunge horror as police question attempted murder suspect CSI were pictured working on a balcony on the top floor View 4 Images Scenes of crime investigators pictured on a top-floor balcony ( News Paul Britton Reporter and Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 12:19, 29 Aug 2026 Updated 14:27, 29 Aug 2026 A man has been arrested on suspicion of the attempted murder of a man who fell from a balcony at a block of flats The suspect, aged in his 20s, was in custody for questioning on Saturday (August 29) as the man who fell, also believed to be in his 20s, was fighting for his life in hospital Police said he was taken to hospital from the scene in Langworthy, Salford , with 'life-threatening injuries' and remained there in a 'critical condition' on Saturday afternoon. Police chiefs said it is believed to be an 'isolated incident' with no wider risk to the public Reports from residents living nearby the scene - a block of flats on Southern Street, off Liverpool Street - said members of the public rushed to help the man who fell and performed CPR on him. It's also claimed the aftermath of the horror was filmed and streamed on TikTok How far the man fell hasn't been confirmed, but specialist scenes of crime investigators were pictured inside the flats on Saturday morning working on a top-floor balcony

candidates.evidence_text: Stockport Stockport council accused of U-turn after plan to increase bin collections Stockport council’s leadership has been accused of ‘making policy on the back of a fag packet’ News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 07:42, 29 Aug 2026 View Ima Stockport council’s leadership has been accused of ‘making policy on the back of a fag packet’ following a major bin announcement. But top councillors said there would be no cuts to services as a result of the change From the beginning of December 2026, blue bins for paper and cardboard recycling will be collected every two weeks instead of every four weeks across Stockport . The council moved to four weekly collections due to financial pressures on its budget for day-to-day services in 2025 Earlier this week, councillor Jake Austin, who is the cabinet member overseeing bin services, said he was delighted to announce the move and feedback had been ‘loud and clear’ that people ‘want a service that makes it easier to recycle’ Council leader Mark Roberts said: “It is critical people know the Liberal Democrats will listen to the feedback given and strive to make a positive difference wherever we can.” The announcement this week has come after weeks of criticism of the local authority . Recent controversial enforcement of a long-standing policy around collecting bins with open lids led to hundreds of people being left with uncollected bins

candidates.evidence_text: The University of Manchester The exact science that could be lost at Jodrell Bank, by a professor of cosmology in the know EXCLUSIVE: 'We would lose our ability to turn the big ideas into something real' Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 08:01, 30 A A leading cosmologist has delivered a worrying insight into the pioneering science and research he says would be lost at Jodrell Bank if funding cuts which threaten the working future of the observatory's Lovell Telescope aren't reversed Phil Bull is a professor of cosmology at the Jodrell Bank Centre for Astrophysics, based at the University of Manchester, and spoke out in support of the Manchester Evening News' campaign to save space science at the site in Cheshire, which has now passed 10,000 signatories Accusing the Government of being misleading in its assessment of exactly what would be affected at Jodrell Bank, he said the cuts would limit the UK's 'ability to turn the big ideas into something real' and lead to the collapse of a key outer space research project SIGN THE MANCHESTER EVENING NEWS CAMPAIGN HERE He argued the loss of funding would bleed into all aspects of work being carried out, 'greatly diminish' research overall at the observatory' and 'remove our ability to pursue a lot of the best and most exciting ideas'

candidates.evidence_text: Health Smelly bedrooms, unclean residents and recruitment concerns in this week's healthcare inspection round-up One GP file held ‘no evidence of qualifications’ News Hannah Richardson 07:57, 30 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Hilltop Court Nursing Home, Heato Greater Manchester services have been pulled up on a number of issues in this week’s healthcare inspection reports Watchdog the Care Quality Commission found residents in a Stockport care home to have dirty hair, nails and clothes. Areas of the service were ‘malodorous’ and people did not always have access to drinks, inspectors added Meanwhile, problems with recruitment were raised at a Platt Bridge GP surgery. One GP file held ‘no evidence of qualifications’, while other missing information included references, proof of identity, DBS checks and employment history documentation. ‘Significant gaps’ in training However, staff at a Manchester home care service were praised by inspectors for their ‘exceptional’ kindness, including throwing a birthday party for a person with no close family. Service users described them as ‘angels’ Here is a breakdown of Greater Manchester’s recently published CQC reports

candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Combined Authority The top boss running Greater Manchester - for now - in £245k role An interim chief has been appointed. News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 07:30, 30 Aug 2026 View 2 Images The Tootal buildings in Manchester An interim top boss has been chosen to run Greater Manchester alongside mayor Bev Craig after the previous chief executive was poached to work in Number 10 North Andrew Lightfoot’s name was put forward on Friday (August 30) to step up from his job as deputy to formally become interim group chief executive at the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA), which also includes Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service The post comes with a wage of £245,000 and serves as the GMCA’s head of paid service - its most senior officer - as well as returning officer and director general of Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) The recommendation needs to be approved on September 25 while the search for a permanent chief begins Former GMCA boss Caroline Simpson stepped down in July to join Andy Burnham's team at Heron House in the Prime Minister’s Manchester office, which opened an ‘immediate gap’ to be plugged at the Combined Authority

candidates.evidence_text: Wigan 'They wouldn't let an animal suffer like this. It's my life, I should be able to choose what happens to it' Brian Griffin has incurable blood cancer. With the assisted dying bill - the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill - set to be debated News Iram Ramzan 07:00, 30 Aug 2026 Updated 07:19, 30 Aug 2026 Standing proud at almost 6ft at his home on a quiet cul-de-sac where he lives with wife Denise, it's hard to believe Brian Griffin is terminally ill. There's little to immediately suggest he is living on borrowed time For decades, Brian was a familiar figure at the front of the classroom, teaching biology and advanced skills to thousands of children across Wigan Among them were his own son and daughter, before he went on to lecture at the University of Manchester . Now the 74-year-old from Bryn is preparing to die, spending much of his remaining days considering how that will happen Brian invited the Manchester Evening News to his home to discuss the assisted dying bill - the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill - which will be debated in the Commons once again next month "If this Bill is passed, then in 30 years' time people will look back thinking 'they just used to let these people suffer - why?'," Brian says. "And I think people will just look back at it as absolutely barbaric."

candidates.evidence_text: Rochdale Taco Bell horror as boy stabbed in toilets after '25 youths ran in with knives' before diners desperately saved victim's life Police cordoned off Taco Bell in Rochdale after the attack with a major investigation underway News Amy Walker Court A 13-year-old boy has been left with serious injuries after being stabbed in Taco Bell in Rochdale . Officers from Greater Manchester Police were called to reports of the serious incident at around 6pm on Saturday, August 19, at the restaurant on Riverside Walk A boy, aged 13, was taken to hospital with serious injuries. Two teenage boys have since been arrested on suspicion of assault and possession of a bladed article. Enquiries are ongoing, GMP say A man and his family, who were dining at the restaurant, witnessed the incident. Speaking to the Manchester Evening News , David Lane told of the 'horrific moment' and how his actions helped save the boy "We sat down and ordered our food at around 5.50pm, then a load of kids came in and started fighting," he said. "I got up and went to one of the crew members at Taco Bell and asked them to kick them out because my family were there "I told them to lock the door, and they never did. About ten minutes later, the crew member who was guarding the door was pushed by one of them, then around 20 to 25 youths ran in, some with knives."

Growing up in Ince-in-Makerfield , one of his earliest recollections of folk-horror-type lore is the childhood memory of Red Clogs – the Wigan bogeyman who haunts the local c The story goes that Red Clogs is the ghost of a tragic miner who was killed in an accident. The legend says the sound of his distinctive clogs could be heard after dark while walking near the old industrial and pit sites “It's interesting because I did a little bit of research when I was writing, and people in different parts of Wigan had a slightly different version of Red Clogs,” David said. “But it was always a spirit or a ghost or a presence that haunted mining communities “And it varied between being a ghost of a miner who was killed or a malevolent spirit who killed people or kidnapped kids. But the unifying feature was where the name came from. Its clogs were red because they were dripping with blood, usually from kicking someone to death

candidates.evidence_text: Salford Man fights for life following Salford flats balcony plunge horror as police question attempted murder suspect CSI were pictured working on a balcony on the top floor View 4 Images Scenes of crime investigators pictured on a top-floor balcony ( News Paul Britton Reporter and Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 12:19, 29 Aug 2026 Updated 14:27, 29 Aug 2026 A man has been arrested on suspicion of the attempted murder of a man who fell from a balcony at a block of flats The suspect, aged in his 20s, was in custody for questioning on Saturday (August 29) as the man who fell, also believed to be in his 20s, was fighting for his life in hospital Police said he was taken to hospital from the scene in Langworthy, Salford , with 'life-threatening injuries' and remained there in a 'critical condition' on Saturday afternoon. It's also claimed the aftermath of the horror was filmed and streamed on TikTok How far the man fell hasn't been confirmed, but specialist scenes of crime investigators were pictured inside the flats on Saturday morning working on a top-floor balcony

candidates.evidence_text: Salford LIVE EVENT ENDED Updated 19 hours ago Salford attempted murder investigation RECAP after man falls from balcony at flats A major investigation is underway The police scene on Liverpool Road, Langworthy, Salford ( Image: Sean Hansford ) News Be Police remained at the scene on Saturday morning (August 29). A man has been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder. The tent is in place beside a block of flats near the Ashley Brook pub on Liverpool Street, where a man plummeted from a balcony He is in hospital with 'life threatening' injuries, Greater Manchester Police said, and is in a critical condition Police tape stretches across the road. Images and video posted to social media show a man being led to a police van in the early hours of Saturday. There are unconfirmed reports of the incident and its aftermath being seen on TikTok Chief Inspector Lee Gridley from GMP's Salford district, said: "We understand that incidents of this nature may cause concern within the community; however, we believe this is an isolated incident and that there is no wider risk to the public "We would like to hear from anyone who may have information that can assist us."

candidates.lead: Stockport Stockport council accused of U-turn after plan to increase bin collections Stockport council’s leadership has been accused of ‘making policy on the back of a fag packet’ News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 07:42, 29 Aug 2026 View Ima Stockport council’s leadersh
candidates.evidence_text: Stockport Stockport council accused of U-turn after plan to increase bin collections Stockport council’s leadership has been accused of ‘making policy on the back of a fag packet’ News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 07:42, 29 Aug 2026 View Ima Stockport council’s leadership has been accused of ‘making policy on the back of a fag packet’ following a major bin announcement. But top councillors said there would be no cuts to services as a result of the change From the beginning of December 2026, blue bins for paper and cardboard recycling will be collected every two weeks instead of every four weeks across Stockport . The council moved to four weekly collections due to financial pressures on its budget for day-to-day services in 2025 Earlier this week, councillor Jake Austin, who is the cabinet member overseeing bin services, said he was delighted to announce the move and feedback had been ‘loud and clear’ that people ‘want a service that makes it easier to recycle’ Council leader Mark Roberts said: “It is critical people know the Liberal Democrats will listen to the feedback given and strive to make a positive difference wherever we can.” The announcement this week has come after weeks of criticism of the local authority . Recent controversial enforcement of a long-standing policy around collecting bins with open lids led to hundreds of people being left with uncollected bins

Four lives lost in a moment. Countless others torn apart Three teenagers and a dad-of-four taxi driver died following a head-on crash on Wigan Road, in Bolton , at 12.45am on Sunday, January 11. Neighbours describe having had multiple cars written off over the years, on a street likened to a 'race track'

Credit: ITV News A major NHS trust has declared a critical incident as more than 350 operating theatre staff begin a series of 24-hour strikes across four hospitals Workers including nurses, clinical support workers, and housekeepers at Salford Royal, Royal Oldham , Rochdale Infirmary, and Fairfield Hospital in Bury are walking out on 24, 26, and 28 August It follows similar strike action taken by staff across the same four hospital sites in June The dispute focuses on the trust using an external agency, NHS Professionals, to manage overtime shifts Trade union UNISON claims this system forces some staff to earn less than a standard shift rate, leaving workers out of pocket by more than £80 per shift when covering staff shortages UNISON Regional Organiser Kevin Dolan claims trust bosses show a "lack of leadership" after an offer was reportedly withdrawn before talks began

Credit: ITV News The new Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig has announced free bus travel for 11-18 year olds on her first day in the job Ms Craig has confirmed the extension of 'Our Pass', which already gives 16-18 year olds free bus travel will take effect from January 2027 Up to 200,000 young people are expected to benefit, in a move which could save families up to £500 a year per child The former Manchester City Council leader was elected on Friday 31 July after winning the election with 47.15% of the vote count. She replaces her friend and now Prime Minister Andy Burnham She said it will help to make getting to education, training and opportunities easier for young people. The Mayor has also revealed dates for new Bee Network bus routes and night buses

candidates.evidence_text: Friday 31 July 2026 at 11:11pm More than two million voters were eligible to vote in the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election as counting getsunderway. Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

Credit: via planning documents Both items on the city council’s planning docket yesterday – a school in Crumpsall and a 1,500-capacity church in Blackley – were given the go-ahead to proceed World Mission Agency was given consent to build a 1,500-capacity church off Chain Road in Blackley for its growing congregation The plans involve the demolition of a former convent located on a 2.5-acre site and the creation of a 57,000 sq ft, two-storey church to replace the current Winners Chapel on Salford’s Broughton Lane The scheme would feature a 10,000 sq ft auditorium for services as well as community facilities such as classrooms and a gym Several objections to the scheme were lodged, many of them raising concerns about the potential for increased traffic congestion due to the number of people using the church

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Plus: Raja Miah vs Herrmann and the Oat Milk Latte Gang Dear readers — welcome to the most important Monday briefing The Mill has ever written, in which we answer the somehow as-yet-unanswered question: how tall really was Mr Manchester? This comes after the news on Saturday that Peter Hook, aka ‘Hooky’ – bassist for Joy Division and known flogger of Factory Records’ corpse – has suggested that what Manchester, nay, Greengate needs is a seven-foot-tall bronze statue of Tony Wilson, looking out over the Irwell tow I'm 5'10" and having met him several times I remember him being marginally but not significantly taller than me We asked every friend or family member of his we have in our contacts, first, what they think of the statue, and also, can you remember how tall he was? The results were similar but inconclusive – so this morning, Ophira and Ethan went to extreme measures to find out once and for But before that, a word from our sponsor. This briefing is brought to you by Herrmann and the Oat Milk Latte Gang: Not an ‘80s synth outfit, but the name bestowed upon us this morning by friend-of-The-Mill Raja Miah

Officers spoke to those at the encampment, who said they intended to leave by Saturday 8th August As the site had not been vacated, the Council returned with support from Greater Manchester Police on Tuesday 11th August. A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. candidates.lead: Thirteen local artists, schools, charities and community groups have been chosen to bring their ideas to life during Oldham’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture
candidates.evidence_text: Thirteen local artists, schools, charities and community groups have been chosen to bring their ideas to life during Oldham’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture From theatre, film and music to a new mural and giant fuzzy felt artwork, the projects cover a wide range of art forms and celebrate Oldham’s people, places and stories Oldham secured the Town of Culture title with its programme, Rising Up . Earlier this year, local creatives were invited to apply for a Town of Culture micro-commission. There were 84 applications, with 13 projects chosen to receive funding Some of the successful artists and groups recently came together to mark the start of the programme. Not everyone was able to attend, but all 13 projects will play an important part in Oldham’s Town of Culture year The Oldham Panorama, a famous view of the town created in 1876, is 150 years old this year. Isobel and Fay will reimagine it for today using patchwork and running-stitch embroidery Local people will be invited to add buildings and places that are important to them, using old clothes and fabric from home

The gank was characterised by tightly packed housing, narrow passageways, high crime rates and large numbers of ‘ The site is so steep that Oldham contractors, Maysand, who delivered the work, had to devise a special pulley system with tracks and rollers to help transport the stone up the hill The team had to painstakingly remove all 122 steps, many of which had become broken and uneven, before reconstructing both the area underneath and the damaged steps using traditional sandstone, to match the existing stone. All materials that were salvageable were recycled and use

evidence_packet.evidence_text: An urgent plea for improved transport links for Leigh has been backed by members of Wigan Council It means Wigan Council will ask Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) and the new Mayor of Greater Manchester to consider ‘interim rapid transport systems’ while long term solutions – such as Metrolink – are assessed Councillor Cunliffe, told colleagues improvements are a “matter of urgency” for residents in and around Leigh, with higher frequency for existing services and smaller scale infrastructure projects required He said: “I know as being part of the Mayoral Development Zone things are happening to see about transport improvement and a feasibility study at getting Metrolink into Leigh. I welcome that “But big infrastructure projects can take years. There are things that can be done in the interim period and that is what we would like to explore.” He added that increased travel times into locations in Manchester city centre and surrounding areas leave residents socially excluded, causing “barriers to employment, education, and social mobility”

candidates.lead: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović .
candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. candidates.evidence_text: Grub on the Docks - Media City UK Street Food Line-Up: Featuring Sizzling Seoul, Dukes Po Boys, and more Grub on the Docks Venue Gardens Dates 28 th May - 20 th Sep '26 Open Tuesday to Sunday weekly, 12 noon – 10pm GRUB on the Docks is bringing the flavour this summer – think unreal street food, ice-cold drinks and non-stop vibes right in the MediaCity gardens, on the waterfront. We’re talking a stacked rotation of indie food like Sizzling Seoul, Umami Cartel, Oppa Korean Dogs and more, switching it up every week so there’s always something new to try. NEW challenge, take on the BELLY BUSTER CHALLENGE from CAFF – sausage. bacon. egg. black pudding. hash brown. All packed into one proper Belly Buster bap for £7.50. Time to beat is 5 minutes set the fastest finishing time and your next Belly Buster is FREE . EVENTS Wine on the Docks Every Wednesday | All day, venue hours Midweek just got better. Every Wednesday, buy two glasses of the same wine and we’ll top up the rest of the bottle on us. No catch, no fuss just a proper reason to make Wednesday your new favourite day. Sunset Sessions Every Friday | 5–8pm Clock off and head straight to the water’s edge. A rotating line-up of DJs kicks off the weekend early, with a trader special and a featured drinks offer to match. Same time, same spot, every Friday, your after-work wind-down sorted. Paws on the Docks 8 AUGUST | 22 AUGUST | 5 SEPTEMBER | 19 SEPTEMBER | Mornings Bring the dog, grab a coffee, make a morning of it. Paws on the Docks is our relaxed dog-friendly social – think breakfast specials, water bowls, complimentary pup cups and market stalls that welcome four-legged visitors as warmly as the two-legged ones. Residents social Thursday 20th August – 5pm to 7pm An evening for all MediaCity residents, with a DJ playing live on the docks. A nice informal social, come down, grab a drink and meet other residents at our waterfront setting. Media Makers Mixer Thursday 27th August – 5pm to 7pm A regular hosted networking event for MediaCity’s creative and production community, designed to bring people together and encourage connections across the area. Be the first in the know Sign up to receive email updates on the latest events, news and offers at MediaCity Visit our privacy policy here. Get yours below and join the party of the year on this May Day Bank Holiday Sunday Chapel Street and the Crescent neighbourhood - see SFTOC website for all venues taking part

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Central Library , Manchester Until 20 December 2026 Additional information Always double check opening hours with the venue before making a special visit Manchester has always been a city with stories to tell. This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

Although the Duck and Drake is now better known From here you’ll venture to the White Swan, a venue linked with one of the city’s oldest music halls, the City Varieties. candidates.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC I rejected a three-year contract from Man United – I made the right decision This defender admitted he had no qualms about turning down a contract from Manchester United Comments Sport Fasika Zelealem 06:00, 30 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Zeki Fryer Zeki Fryers knows what it's like to play for Manchester United and to reject them The former academy graduate has played for 11 clubs since leaving Old Trafford , including their Premier League opponents on Sunday, Ipswich Town. Для многих украинцев за границей ее концерт станет не только художественным Наталья Карпа получила два высших образования, однако именно музыка стала делом ее жизни. От первых фестивалей и конкурсов до больших сцен Украины и мира, от песни “Калина”, открывшей ей путь к широкому признанию, до многочисленных сольных концертов и международных туров для укра Заслуженная артистка Украины, автор десятков популярных композиций, продюсер и общественный деятель в своем репертуаре легко сочетает лирическую нежность и праздничную энергию, а рядом с хорошо известными хитами непременно звучат новые композиции. Недаром поклонники после концерт В Лондоне прозвучат песни, сопровождавшие разные поколения украинцев, будут звучать слова, в которых живут любовь, вера и несокрушимость. Музыка преодолевает расстояния, находит дорогу к сердцу независимо от того, где человек живет сегодня, и оставляет после себя огонь жизни! Чтобы попасть на концерт Наталки Карпы в Лондоне, покупайте билеты на нашем сайте и в кассах города. Еще больше концертов в афише Лондона ищите у нас на сайте

For example, a parcel containing products under different tariff headings may attract multiple While the change is aimed largely at addressing the growth of low-value e-commerce imports, it will also impact UK businesses selling products directly into EU markets, including online retailers, brands and SMEs What the new €3 EU customs duty means for UK businesses
